subject: Service credit thresholds & latency carve-outs — CloudGrove template negotiation
messages:
From: Sam Patel <spatel@cloudgrove.io>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: CloudGrove Legal <legal@cloudgrove.io>
Date: Mon, 10 Mar 2025 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: SLA ask — monthly credit caps and tighter latency SLOs

Irene,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We are working through the contract with procurement and legal — two items they pushed back on that I'd like to resolve this week so we can move to signature:

1) Standard uptime: your template lists 99.95% for the Hosted plan. Given our low-latency inference needs in the EU, procurement is asking if we can get the baseline raised to 99.98% (or a tighter remediation ladder) or, alternatively, a higher monthly service credit cap if the uptime drops below 99.98%.

2) Latency cures: we need a P95 latency SLO for the inference endpoint under normal load (target P95 < 200ms). If that SLO is missed, they want a defined monthly credit band tied to severity (e.g., X% credit for 2–4 p95 misses, Y% for >4).

I've attached a short request doc that their legal team provided with examples of acceptable credit caps and carve-outs. Can Redwood confirm what you can offer for CloudGrove EU (region) and whether we can keep maintenance carve-outs consistent with GDPR change windows?

Timeline: procurement would like redlines by Friday 14 Mar so we can route to finance.

Best,
Sam Patel
Head of PlatformOps, CloudGrove
[attachment: CloudGrove_SLA_Request.pdf (pdf)]

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <spatel@cloudgrove.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Mar 2025 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA ask — monthly credit caps and tighter latency SLOs

Sam — thanks for the clear notes and the attachment. Internal summary below and a proposed compromise in the attached annex.

Short answer: we can accommodate a tighter uptime guardrail for an EU-specific commitment, but it will be scoped to a committed configuration and a modest uplift in contract economics (we list options below). We can also define a latency remediation ladder for P95 misses with capped dollar exposure.

Proposal (high level):
- Baseline uptime: 99.95% across hosted by default. For CloudGrove EU we can commit to a regional SLA of 99.98% for the Core Inference route if you sign a regional reservation (12-month minimum).
- Monthly service credit cap: capped at 100% of the monthly service fee for availability failures (classic model), with a separate latency remediation pool that pays up to 50% of the monthly fee for recurrent P95 violations.
- Latency SLO: P95 < 200ms under normal load (definition in Annex A). Severity ladder in Annex B: first 1–2 months with single-day blips = advisory; 2–4 months with repeated P95 breaches = 10% credit (per month); >4 months with repeated breaches = 25% credit (per month) — credit applied from the latency pool.
- Maintenance carve-outs: scheduled maintenance windows (published 7 days ahead) excluded; emergency maintenance limited to documented incident response and mutually agreedation on scope.

I've attached an SLA_Annex-Draft.docx with language we commonly use and a clean markup for the regional commitment option. If you prefer not to take the reservation, we can keep 99.95% and increase the monthly credit cap to 150% for the first 6 months as a transitional remedy.

Next step: Can we do a 30-minute alignment call tomorrow (Tue 11 Mar) with procurement to walk through the annex and economics? If you sign off on the regional reservation option we'll include the redline for DocuSign.

Thanks — Irene
Irene Choi
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[attachment: SLA_Annex-Draft.docx (docx)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Mar 2025 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA ask — monthly credit caps and tighter latency SLOs

Irene / Ben — quick internal notes before we lock the annex: our levers here are (a) regional reservation (12m commit) and (b) how we split availability vs latency pools. My suggestions:

1) Keep availability cap at 100% monthly fee for availability failures — that's standard and legal prefers this.
2) For latency remedial credits, cap at 50% of monthly spend but make the trigger non-trivial: require at least 2 distinct weekly measurement periods with P95 > 200ms before any payout, to avoid noisy single-day spikes counting.
3) Add a 6-month pilot clause: if CloudGrove signs reservation, put a 6-month review clause where we measure observed p95 and adjust thresholds if their traffic pattern shows sustained bursts (we can use our telemetry to provide a monthly report).

Ben — can you confirm if the engineering ops team is comfortable with the proposed measurement windows (we prefer UTC day boundaries and a 3-day smoothing window for P95 calculations)? If yes we'll push this back to Sam and present the reservation economics (small uplift on committed rate).

Laura
VP, Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference

From: Sam Patel <spatel@cloudgrove.io>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: CloudGrove Legal <legal@cloudgrove.io>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 Mar 2025 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA ask — monthly credit caps and tighter latency SLOs

Irene — appreciate the quick turnaround and the annex. We discussed internally and CloudGrove is willing to accept the regional reservation path (12 months) with the 99.98% EU commitment and the latency ladder you proposed, provided the measurement gating Laura suggested (2 distinct weekly measurement periods before payout) is included.

We also want the 6-month pilot review clause to be explicit and for Redwood to provide the monthly telemetry report (P95, request volumes, tail events) for the pilot period. Once those three items are included, legal asked for a single redline pass and DocuSign.

Please share a redlined PDF or DocuSign envelope and we'll route for signature on our side. Happy to take the 30-min call if that helps finalize wording.

Thanks,
Sam Patel
Head of PlatformOps, CloudGrove
